To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the intrinsic fluctuations in the threshold voltage and the drain current of minimum size transistors in a 6T CMOS SRAM are the primary cause for the degradation in the static noise margin (SMM).

the impact of threshold voltage fluctuations in minimum geometry CMOS SRAM cells is significant and can be mitigated by increasing the number of devices per bit, by using multiple supply voltages, or by employing new cell architectures.

(i) the SNM of a 6T SRAMS is highly sensitive to intrinsic device fluctuations, which can lead to significant degradation of the SNM of the SRAM cell, and (ii) the impact of intrinsic fluctuations on the SNM of SRAM cells increases with scaling of technology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel low voltage, low leakage, high density SRAM memory cells for future CMOS technology generations.
the fundamental limitations of CMOS scaling and the impact of these limitations on the design and performance of CMOS SRAM cells.
the impact of device parameter fluctuations on CMOS static random access memory (SRAM) cell static noise margin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intrinsic threshold voltage fluctuations alone are projected as a major barrier to the continued scaling of CMOS SRAM cells and the associated CMOS ASICs.
the intrinsic threshold voltage fluctuations are a major limiting factor for CMOS SRAM scaling.

the intrinsic device fluctuations in minimum geometry CMOS SRAM cells are projected to exceed nominal SNM for sub 100nm CMOS technology generations and pose severe barriers to the scaling of supply voltage and transistor count for CMOS ASICs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
intrinsic device fluctuations are a major limiting factor for scaling of CMOS technology and that new SRAM cell designs are needed to overcome this problem.

, for sub 100nm CMOS technology generations, the intrinsic threshold voltage fluctuations alone will pose severe limitations to scaling of supply, channel length, threshold voltage, and transistor count.
the intrinsic threshold voltage fluctuations are a fundamental limit to scaling the SRAM static noise margin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the impact of threshold voltage fluctuations on SRAM cell static stability is significant and will continue to be a major concern for future CMOS technologies.

SRAM cell stability is not just a function of device dimensions, supply voltage, and operating temperature, but is strongly dependent upon device threshold voltage fluctuations, which are a direct result of device scaling.
the impact of intrinsic device parameter fluctuations is a significant barrier to scaling of SRAM cell stability, which must be addressed to achieve the full potential of CMOS scaling.
